newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Matav takes Merrill Lynch as adviser on possible IPO.
newsitem.headline: Matav takes Merrill Lynch as adviser on possible IPO.

text.p: Hungarian telecommunications company Matav said on Thursday it had chosen Merrill Lynch as financial adviser and global coordinator for a potential IPO.

Matav, which holds a monopoly on ground telecommunications in Hungary, has not announced officially that it will go through with the offering, but analysts have said it may sell a stake of up to 17 percent.
Merrill Lynch was chosen by Matav's board of directors at a meeting on Thursday, the company said in a statement.
Matav is 67 percent owned by a 50-50 consortium of Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech Corp, while the state holds a 25 percent stake and the rest is held by a variety of investors.
If the state decides to sell its entire stake, the offering could be valued as high as $1 billion and would be Hungary's biggest public offering to date, analysts said.
